title.en: The Raven and the Fox: the story in brief

text.en:
Ravi's friend praised him loudly and then asked for his lunch.
"Be careful of sweet talk," said his mother.

This is the old fable of a raven and a fox. The raven sits on a branch holding a piece of food in its beak. A hungry fox sees it and starts to praise the raven's looks and voice.
The raven, pleased, opens its beak to sing, and the food drops to the ground. The fox picks it up and goes away.
The lesson is to be careful of flattery, which is praise that is not sincere. This summary is based on the well-known story or poem and on public chapter notes. Please read the exact text in the textbook, because the textbook version may differ in details.
